newsitem.title: UK: British unemployment falls 41,100 in March.
newsitem.headline: British unemployment falls 41,100 in March.

text.p: British unemployment in March fell by 41,100 to 1.71 million, its thirteenth successive monthly decline, according to official figures published on Wednesday.
The unemployment rate fell to 6.1 percent of the workforce, compared with 6.2 percent in February.
The number of people out of work was the lowest since September 1990.
Average earnings in February rose by five percent, compared with a rise of 4.75 percent the porevious month.
Economist Andrew Snowball of the Cooperative Bank said the figures were broadly in line with expectations. "On balance, a broadly positive set of numbers," he told Reuters.

Britain's opposition Labour Party said that if it won the May 1 election it would review how the jobless figures are compiled. Media reports say the government admits privately the figures currently understate the level of unemployment.
